title: Choose the visual world for CodeBreakers
question: Your Star Trek / Helldivers brief is fixed. The roll picked which part of that world carries the game: keep the War Table, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Galactic War Table
options.lineage: the holo war table on a starship command deck
options.thesis: The whole game is played on the ship's war table: worlds are sectors you liberate with code, and every mission is projected onto the same table.
materials: gunmetal console rails with warm color-block elbows
hologram light only on the table
options.viewport: A 3/4 view of the war table with five Blender-made 3D planets in orbit, a console rail for Campaign / Arcade / Combat / Teacher, and one hazard-yellow Deploy.
options.risk: The spectacle could compete with the code editor, so the table must recede while the player is coding.

raised.raise: Hazard yellow is reserved for things you can press; disabled actions lose it entirely.
A world or mission that changes state updates in place and holds its highlight until the player opens it.
Each world owns fixed furniture: name plate, one-line skill note, liberation meter.
Console motion is mechanical: short stepped transitions, no floaty fades.
Panels never reflow on state change; only values flip inside fixed cells with tabular numerals.

options.label: Stratagem Call-in HUD
options.lineage: a drop trooper's helmet HUD and arrow-code call-ins
options.thesis: Every program is a stratagem code: the arrow queue is entered like a call-in sequence and thrown onto the grid.
options.viewport: Mission-first: the 7x7 grid fills the view as a top-down tactical feed, the arrow-code strip runs along the bottom, the editor slides out as a terminal.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of the brief; the Star Trek half nearly disappears.

options.label: Star Lane Diagram
options.thesis: Each world is a colored hyperspace lane and every mission is a station on it; progress reads like a route map.
options.viewport: The full five-lane network with the next station ringed; tapping a station opens its briefing beside the map.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and is the clearest progress map, but players identify less with a transit chart than with a starship.
options.risk: Drifts away from the Star Trek / Helldivers brief unless the lanes are dressed as starship navigation.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, plain labels, one action color.
options.viewport: A scrolling column of mission cards with a bottom tab bar.
options.case: Loses both axes: it ignores the brief and flattens the campaign.
options.kept: One action color, used only where something can be pressed.

options.label: Boarding Pass + Gate Board
options.thesis: Missions as flights reranking on a live board.
options.viewport: A departures board of missions ordered by readiness.
options.case: Loses both axes against the war table.
options.kept: State changes move in place and stay lit until noticed.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Worlds as a ranked cast of mascots.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of world mascots.
options.risk: Too young for senior high players.
options.case: Loses both axes for this audience.
options.kept: Each world gets fixed personal furniture: name plate and one-line note.

options.label: Acetate Manual Tab Board
options.thesis: A tabbed manual with acetate leaves over colored boards.
options.viewport: An open manual at the current world's tab.
options.risk: Print metaphor fights the bridge console.
options.case: Loses both axes; strong only for the code reference.
options.kept: Mechanical motion: short stepped changes, no easing fades.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.kept: Fixed cells; values change, layout never reflows.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark sci-fi game menu: centered logo, glowing buttons over a starfield, card grids for modes.
canonCard.viewport: Logo and a stack of glowing buttons centered over space art.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other space game, and close to what the file already has.
